- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., after 75+ values), then corrects with a downward bias in later days.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or lagged adjustment.
- Forecasts tend to be too high relative to recent 7–14 day moving average, indicating failure to capture short-term momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the 30-day forecast, especially when history shows consolidation or downward trend.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model overreacts with exaggerated peak, then underreacts in the tail.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–3% for the last 5–10 days to account for mean reversion or market cooling.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in first 5 days, reduce subsequent forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overcorrection.
- Model fails to adjust for recent volatility clustering — should apply smoothing or volatility-weighted decay to forecasts.
